key_terms.meaning: Android interface giving an app a small private key-value store that Android saves as one XML file in the app's data folder.
Context method that opens or creates a preferences file with the given name and returns a SharedPreferences object.
Access mode that makes the preferences file readable only by the app that created it; it is the normal choice.
Methods that write pending preference edits; apply() writes in the background and commit() writes at once and returns true or false.
Private folder owned by the app, path from getFilesDir(), always available and removed when the app is uninstalled.
Shared storage space, path from getExternalFilesDir(), which may be missing when the SD card or emulated volume is unmounted.
Internal folder for temporary files that the system may delete when storage runs low.
Android rule that limits an app to its own external directories plus media or documents the user explicitly grants.
Abstract helper class that creates the database the first time it is opened and calls onUpgrade when the version number rises.
Helper callbacks where you write the CREATE TABLE statements and the ALTER or migrate statements.
Object that runs SQL and helper methods such as insert(), query(), update() and delete() on one database file.
Pointer to the result rows of a query; it starts before the first row and moves with moveToNext().
Column name Android requires for lists such as ListView adapters; use it as the primary key name or alias it as _id.
App component that publishes a data set under a content:// URI so other apps can read or write it through a fixed API.
Address of provider data, shaped content://authority/path/id, where authority names the provider and id names one row.
Client-side object, obtained with getContentResolver(), that sends query, insert, update and delete calls to the provider that owns a URI.
Helper that maps incoming URIs to integer codes so one provider can serve several URI shapes, like all rows or one row.
Intent flag giving the receiving app temporary read access to the content:// URI placed in that intent.
Ready-made content provider in AndroidX that shares files as content:// URIs instead of file:// paths.
Library that links a data object to a layout so the view redraws when the object changes, without findViewById and setText.

takeaways: SharedPreferences holds a few key-value settings in one private XML file; it is not a place for lists of records or large data.
Internal storage is private and always present, external storage is shared and may be unmounted, so check availability before writing.
SQLiteOpenHelper keeps the create and upgrade logic in one class, so every part of the app opens the same database the same way.
A Cursor is a window over the result rows; read the column indexes once and close the Cursor when the work is done.
A content provider hides your tables behind a content:// URI, so other apps never touch your files directly.
ContentResolver is the client half of the same contract: your own app should also read provider data through it.
Share data by sending a content:// URI with a temporary grant flag, never by giving out a raw file path.
Data binding removes the findViewById and setText glue; change the model and the bound views update on their own.
bank_note: Long answers here are graded on the full chain: the create-and-upgrade code for SQLite, the provider contract with URIs and UriMatcher, the resolver call on the client side, and the safety of the sharing intent.

bank.q: Explain SharedPreferences. How is the data stored, how do you read it back, and what kind of data should not go into it?
outline: Key-value store, one XML file in the app's private data folder
getSharedPreferences(name, MODE_PRIVATE) then getString, getInt and so on with a default value
Edit, put, then apply() or commit()
Not for large data, lists of records or secrets that must be encrypted

bank.q: Compare internal storage and external storage in Android with respect to privacy, availability, permission and lifetime after uninstall.
outline: getFilesDir() private and always available; getExternalFilesDir() shared and can be unmounted
Scoped storage limits what an app may touch on external storage
Check Environment.getExternalStorageState() before writing
Internal files are deleted on uninstall; app-specific external files also go on uninstall but the rest of the card does not
Cache folder is temporary and can be cleared by the system

bank.q: Describe SQLiteOpenHelper. Explain its constructor parameters and the roles of onCreate() and onUpgrade().
outline: Constructor takes Context, database name, CursorFactory, version
getWritableDatabase() and getReadableDatabase() open or create the file
onCreate runs once when the file does not exist and holds CREATE TABLE statements
onUpgrade runs when the stored version is lower than the new one; old data must be migrated or tables recreated
factory is usually null; it can create custom Cursors

bank.q: What is a content provider? Explain its main methods and the parts of a content:// URI.
outline: Provider is an app component declared in the manifest with an authority
Methods: onCreate, query, insert, update, delete, getType
URI form content://authority/path/id
Authority identifies the provider, path identifies a table or collection, id identifies one row
Clients use ContentResolver rather than the provider class directly

bank.q: Explain data binding in Android: enabling it, the layout change, and the generated binding class.
outline: Enable with buildFeatures dataBinding true in the module build file
Wrap the layout in a layout tag with a data block
Declare a variable with name and type
Generated binding class named from the layout file, inflate with DataBindingUtil
Set the variable and the expressions update the views

bank.q: Write the Java or Kotlin code for a settings screen that saves a user name and a high-score integer in SharedPreferences and reads them back at startup, showing the default when nothing is stored.
outline: Get SharedPreferences with MODE_PRIVATE
Use edit(), putString, putInt, apply()
Read with getString(key, default) and getInt(key, default)
Correct types and key constants
No commit() on the main thread in a tight loop

bank.q: Write a SQLiteOpenHelper subclass for a notes table with columns _id, title and body. Show the CREATE TABLE statement and one method that inserts a note and one that returns all notes as a Cursor.
outline: Table with _id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT
onCreate executes CREATE TABLE, onUpgrade handles the version change
ContentValues for insert through insert()
query() with null selection or db.rawQuery
Cursor returned, column names read with getColumnIndexOrThrow

bank.q: Write a content provider for a student table. Show the authority, the UriMatcher with codes for all rows and a single row, and the query() and insert() methods.
outline: Manifest provider entry with android:authorities
UriMatcher addURI for content://authority/students and .../students/#
query() switches on match, sets the notification URI, returns the Cursor
insert() puts values, inserts, notifies listeners, returns the new row URI
getType() returns the correct MIME type

bank.q: Show how one app shares an image file with another app using a content:// URI and an intent, including the manifest and XML needed for FileProvider.
outline: FileProvider declared with authority and meta-data pointing to a paths XML file
Build the URI with FileProvider.getUriForFile
ACTION_SEND intent with type image/*, EXTRA_STREAM and FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION
Receiver uses ContentResolver.openInputStream
No file:// URI, since that throws FileUriExposedException on newer Android

bank.q: Convert an existing findViewByid and setText screen into a data-bound screen. Show the model class, the layout with the variable and the activity code.
outline: Plain model class or ObservableField for change notification
layout and data block with the variable
@{student.name} style expressions in the views
Binding class inflated with DataBindingUtil.setContentView
binding.setStudent(model) replaces findViewById and setText

bank.q: A to-do app must store a theme choice, an offline list of 5,000 tasks, a downloaded photo and one setting shared with a widget in another app. Choose a storage mechanism for each need and justify the choice.
outline: Theme choice goes to SharedPreferences, tiny and read at startup
Tasks go to SQLite, needs queries, sorting and partial updates
Photo goes to internal or app-specific external storage, with the path kept in a table column
Shared setting goes behind a content provider read through ContentResolver
Justify by size, query needs, privacy and lifetime, not by habit

bank.q: Examine the security risks of sharing data between apps. Evaluate android:exported, URI permission flags and input validation in the provider.
outline: Exported provider is reachable by any app; declare only when needed
FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION grants one URI for one receiving app and can be revoked
Provider must validate the URI and use parameterised queries through selectionArgs to avoid SQL injection
Check caller permission with checkCallingPermission where data is sensitive
Never expose a whole table when a single row URI is enough

bank.q: Your app version 2 adds a new column to a table already installed on users' phones. Analyse the upgrade paths and recommend one, stating the risk of each.
outline: Bump the version number in the SQLiteOpenHelper constructor
onUpgrade with ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN keeps existing rows
Drop and recreate loses user data but is simple
Use oldVersion and newVersion in switch or if chains so users skipping versions still migrate
Back up or export data before destructive migration; test with an installed older build

bank.q: Compare SharedPreferences, files, SQLite and a content provider as persistence choices, and explain why a provider adds value even when only your own app reads the data.
outline: Size, structure, query ability, privacy and sharing for each option
Preferences for a few settings, files for blobs, SQLite for structured records
Provider gives a stable URI contract that survives table changes
Resolver keeps UI code away from database code and allows loaders or cursor adapters
Cost: extra code and IPC overhead, so skip it for tiny private data

bank.q: A list screen built with a CursorAdapter is slow and leaks. Analyse the likely causes and evaluate fixes, naming the Cursor methods involved.
outline: Query on the main thread; move to a background thread or use a loader
Cursor never closed; close in onDestroy or when swapped
moveToNext and getColumnIndex called inside every bind instead of caching indexes
_id column missing, so the adapter cannot work
Requeries after insert using the notification URI

glossary.def: One saved setting stored as a key with a value of a simple type.
Storage where each value is found by a unique key rather than by position.
SharedPreferences.Editor object that collects put calls and writes them on apply() or commit().
Value returned by a preference read when the key has never been saved.
Folders owned by one app, inside internal or external storage, cleared when the app is uninstalled.
Context method returning the absolute path of the app's private internal files folder.
Context method returning an app-specific folder on external storage, or null if it is not mounted.
Temporary files the system may delete when storage is low.
Android rule that an app reaches only its own external folders plus user-granted media or documents.
Small embedded relational database engine that stores a whole database in one file.
The declared structure of a database: its tables, columns, types and constraints.
Column whose value uniquely identifies each row of a table.
Key-value map of column names to values, passed to insert() and update().
Object holding a query result set and a position, moved with moveToNext() and read with getString() or getInt().
Required column name for Android list adapters; a primary key named id can be aliased as _id.
App component that exposes a data set to other apps under a content:// URI.
Unique name of a provider, usually a reverse domain string, the first part after content://.
Client object that finds the provider for a URI and forwards query, insert, update and delete calls.
Class that maps a URI pattern to a numeric code so a provider can branch on the URI shape.
String such as vnd.android.cursor.dir/vnd.authority.table returned by getType() to describe the data a URI points to.
Temporary access to one content:// URI given to a receiving app through an intent flag.
AndroidX content provider that turns a private file into a shareable content:// URI.
Library that lets layout expressions read a data object and refresh the views when it changes.
Generated class named from the layout file, holding references to the views and the bound variables.
